raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Summary Adds an opt-in path to route the DeepSeek-R1 attention output projection (o_proj) MXFP4 GEMM through aiter's ASM a4w4 kernel (gemm_a4w4) instead of the default triton kernel (gemm_afp4wfp4). Only the o_proj linear is affected; all other MXFP4 linears and MoE layers are untouched. When enabled, the layer: converts its serialized (triton-layout) packed weight + e8m0 block-scale into the ASM preshuffled layout once at load time, and quantizes the activation with dynamic_mxfp4_quant(shuffle=True) and calls gemm_a4w4(..., bpreshuffle=True) at runtime. The MLA fused-decode path is updated to skip its triton pre-quant for an ASM o_proj so the layer receives a plain bf16 activation. The feature falls back to the triton kernel if the aiter ASM build is unavailable. Also adds a CPU unit test covering the routing gate. ## Microbench results | M | triton µs | asm µs | speedup | asm_vs_tri_max_abs | |-----:|----------:|-------:|--------:|-------------------:| | 4 | 15.57 | 26.19 | 0.59× | 0.000 | | 64 | 23.17 | 28.59 | 0.81× | 0.000 | | 128 | 26.53 | 28.25 | 0.94× | 0.000 | | 256 | 39.25 | 32.85 | 1.20× | 0.000 | | 512 | 57.70 | 44.19 | 1.31× | 0.000 | | 864 | 89.49 | 62.89 | 1.42× | 0.000 | | 1024 | 93.10 | 66.13 | 1.41× | 0.000 | For smaller batch sizes the triton kernel is more efficient but for larger batch sizes >=256 the asm implementation gives significant gains. This justifies the addition of a flag to decide if the user wants to enable the asm implementation or not depending on his batch size of interest. For MLPerf, where the decode batch size operating point is around 900-1000, this gives significant gains. The last column is an accuracy test which shows that the asm and triton kernel outputs are bit exact. So the asm kernel provides a pure speed benefit with no accuracy regression (with respect to the mxfp4 triton kernel) at higher batch sizes. ## End-to-End results ### Performance | 8×MI355X | DP8/TP8 | ISL/OSL 1024/1024 | num_prompts = 5× concurrency | Concurrency (per-GPU M) | Kernel | Output tok/s | Total tok/s | Peak output tok/s | Duration (s) | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | Median E2E (ms) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 4096 (~512/rank) | triton | 9511.57 | 19023.15 | 27652 | 2204.84 | 408.00 | 214.97 | 444681.4 | | 4096 (~512/rank) | asm | 11111.61 | 22223.21 | 30175 | 1887.35 | 347.32 | 176.01 | 379698.2 | Asm kernel gives ~17% performance boost over Triton kernel ### Accuracy: GSM8K (DeepSeek-R1 MXFP4, 8×MI355X, 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy) | Kernel | Accuracy | Invalid | Correct (of 1319) | Eval latency (s) | |---|---|---|---|---| | triton (SGLANG_DSR_OPROJ_MXFP4_ASM=0) | 0.952 | 0.000 | ~1256 | 31.6 | | asm (SGLANG_DSR_OPROJ_MXFP4_ASM=1) | 0.950 | 0.000 | ~1253 | 32.2 | | **Δ (asm − triton)** | **−0.002** | 0 | ~−3 | — | Accuracy between the 2 fp4 kernels is nearly identical ## Validation The trace shows the asm kernel getting picked up instead of the triton mxfp4 kernel when the flag is enabled. ## Modifications ### Feature (opt-in via `SGLANG_DSR_OPROJ_MXFP4_ASM=1`) - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/quark.py`** (+11): in `get_linear_scheme`, flip a `*.o_proj` `QuarkW4A4MXFP4` scheme into ASM mode (`enable_asm()`) when the env var is set. - **`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py`** (+66): import aiter ASM entry points (`gemm_a4w4`, `shuffle_weight`, `dynamic_mxfp4_quant`, `e8m0_shuffle`) guarded with a triton fallback; add `enable_asm()`; preshuffle the weight + e8m0 block-scale into the ASM layout at load time (`process_weights_after_loading`, tags `mxfp4_use_asm=True`); add the ASM branch in `apply_weights` (activation `dynamic_mxfp4_quant(shuffle=True)` + `gemm_a4w4(bpreshuffle=True)`). - **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mla.py`** (+5/-2): in the MLA absorb path, skip the triton `fused_flatten_mxfp4_quant` pre-quant for an ASM `o_proj` so it receives a plain bf16 activation. ## Tests - **`test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_oproj_asm.py`** (+120): CPU-only unit test for the routing gate (no model, no kernels — aiter availability is mocked): - `enable_asm()` flips to ASM mode only on HIP with the aiter ASM kernel available, otherwise stays on triton. - `get_linear_scheme()` routes to ASM only for `*.o_proj` when `SGLANG_DSR_OPROJ_MXFP4_ASM=1`, and leaves other layers / env-unset / env=`0` on triton. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #30799864391](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30799864391) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30799864114](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30799864114)

## Code Review

This pull request introduces an opt-in mechanism to route DeepSeek attention output projection (o_proj) layers through the aiter ASM a4w4 MXFP4 GEMM kernel on HIP devices when the SGLANG_DSR_OPROJ_MXFP4_ASM environment variable is enabled. The changes include weight preshuffling at load time, integration with the MLA forward path, and unit tests. The review feedback highlights critical improvements: ensuring weight and scale tensors are contiguous before viewing them, updating parameter data in-place to preserve custom parameter classes, asserting against unsupported pre-quantized tuple inputs in the ASM path to prevent silent correctness bugs, and using the idiomatic get_bool_env_var helper for environment variable parsing.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.
> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

There are two important improvements to make here:
1. Calling `.view(torch.uint8)` on `layer.weight.data` and `layer.weight_scale.data` can raise a `RuntimeError` if the tensors are not contiguous (e.g., due to slicing or sharding during tensor parallel loading). Calling `.contiguous()` first prevents this.
2. Recreating `layer.weight` and `layer.weight_scale` as plain `torch.nn.Parameter` objects discards their original custom parameter classes (`PackedvLLMParameter` and `GroupQuantScaleParameter`) and any associated custom attributes/metadata (such as `input_dim`, `output_dim`, `packed_dim`, etc.). This can break downstream components or tensor parallel communication that rely on these custom parameter types. Instead, update the parameter data in-place by assigning to `.data`.

```python
            weight = layer.weight.data.contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
            weight_scale = layer.weight_scale.data.contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
            weight = _asm_shuffle_weight(weight, layout=(16, 16))
            weight_scale = _asm_e8m0_shuffle(weight_scale)
            layer.weight.data = weight.contiguous()
            layer.weight_scale.data = weight_scale.contiguous()
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

If `self.use_asm` is `True` but `x` is a tuple (indicating a pre-quantized input), the code currently silently falls through to the Triton GEMM path. However, because the weights and scales have already been preshuffled for the ASM kernel during loading, running the Triton GEMM on these shuffled weights will produce completely incorrect results (silent correctness bug). We should explicitly assert or raise an error if `x` is a tuple when `self.use_asm` is enabled.

```suggestion
        if self.use_asm:
            assert not isinstance(x, tuple), "ASM path does not support pre-quantized tuple inputs."
            out_features = layer.weight.shape[0]
            if x.dim() == 3:
                out_shape = (*x.shape[:-1], out_features)
                x = x.view(-1, x.shape[-1])
            else:
                out_shape = (x.shape[0], out_features)
            x_q, x_s = _asm_dynamic_mxfp4_quant(x, shuffle=True)
            y = _asm_gemm_a4w4(
                x_q,
                layer.weight,
                x_s,
                layer.weight_scale,
                bpreshuffle=True,
            )
            if bias is not None:
                y = y + bias
            return y.view(*out_shape)
```

+  layers when the env var is set to "1".
+"""
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.quark.quark import QuarkConfig
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.quark.schemes import quark_w4a4_mxfp4 as mxfp4_mod
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.quark.schemes.quark_w4a4_mxfp4 import QuarkW4A4MXFP4
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+
+def _bare_scheme() -> QuarkW4A4MXFP4:
+    """Build a scheme without running __init__ (needs no config for the gate)."""
+    scheme = QuarkW4A4MXFP4.__new__(QuarkW4A4MXFP4)
+    scheme.use_asm = False
+    return scheme
+
+
+def _bare_config() -> QuarkConfig:
+    return QuarkConfig.__new__(QuarkConfig)
+
+
+class TestEnableAsm(CustomTestCase):
+    """`QuarkW4A4MXFP4.enable_asm()` availability handling."""
+
+    def test_enabled_when_asm_available(self):
+        scheme = _bare_scheme()
+        with patch.object(mxfp4_mod, "_is_hip", True), patch.object(
+            mxfp4_mod, "_HAS_ASM_A4W4", True
+        ):
+            scheme.enable_asm()
+        self.assertTrue(scheme.use_asm)
+
+    def test_falls_back_when_asm_missing(self):
+        scheme = _bare_scheme()
+        with patch.object(mxfp4_mod, "_is_hip", True), patch.object(
+            mxfp4_mod, "_HAS_ASM_A4W4", False
+        ):
+            scheme.enable_asm()
+        self.assertFalse(scheme.use_asm)
+
+    def test_falls_back_when_not_hip(self):
+        scheme = _bare_scheme()
+        with patch.object(mxfp4_mod, "_is_hip", False), patch.object(
+            mxfp4_mod, "_HAS_ASM_A4W4", True
+        ):
+            scheme.enable_asm()
+        self.assertFalse(scheme.use_asm)
+
+
+class TestGetLinearSchemeRouting(CustomTestCase):
+    """The `get_linear_scheme` opt-in gate only fires for o_proj + env=1."""
+
+    def _run(self, layer_name: str, env_value):
+        """Return the scheme produced by get_linear_scheme for layer_name.
+
+        The scheme-selection internals are mocked so the test isolates the
+        env/o_proj gate; enable_asm() is exercised for real with ASM forced
+        available. `env_value` is passed to the env flag's override() context.
+        """
+        config = _bare_config()
+        scheme = _bare_scheme()
+
+        with patch.object(
+            QuarkConfig, "_find_matched_config", return_value={}
+        ), patch.object(
+            QuarkConfig, "_get_scheme_from_config", return_value=scheme
+        ), patch.object(
+            QuarkConfig, "_check_scheme_supported", return_value=True
+        ), patch.object(
+            scheme, "get_min_capability", return_value=70
+        ), patch.object(
+            mxfp4_mod, "_is_hip", True
+        ), patch.object(
+            mxfp4_mod, "_HAS_ASM_A4W4", True
+        ), envs.SGLANG_DSR_OPROJ_MXFP4_ASM.override(
+            env_value
+        ):
+            return config.get_linear_scheme(layer=None, layer_name=layer_name)
+
+    def test_oproj_with_env_enables_asm(self):
+        scheme = self._run("model.layers.3.self_attn.o_proj", True)
+        self.assertTrue(scheme.use_asm)
+
+    def test_oproj_env_disabled_keeps_triton(self):
+        scheme = self._run("model.layers.3.self_attn.o_proj", False)
+        self.assertFalse(scheme.use_asm)
+
+    def test_oproj_env_zero_string_keeps_triton(self):
+        scheme = self._run("model.layers.3.self_attn.o_proj", "0")
+        self.assertFalse(scheme.use_asm)
+
+    def test_oproj_unset_keeps_triton(self):
+        config = _bare_config()
+        scheme = _bare_scheme()
+        envs.SGLANG_DSR_OPROJ_MXFP4_ASM.clear()
+        with patch.object(
+            QuarkConfig, "_find_matched_config", return_value={}
+        ), patch.object(
+            QuarkConfig, "_get_scheme_from_config", return_value=scheme
+        ), patch.object(
+            QuarkConfig, "_check_scheme_supported", return_value=True
+        ), patch.object(
+            scheme, "get_min_capability", return_value=70
+        ), patch.object(
+            mxfp4_mod, "_is_hip", True
+        ), patch.object(
+            mxfp4_mod, "_HAS_ASM_A4W4", True
+        ):
+            scheme = config.get_linear_scheme(
+                layer=None, layer_name="model.layers.3.self_attn.o_proj"
+            )
+        self.assertFalse(scheme.use_asm)
+
+    def test_non_oproj_with_env_keeps_triton(self):
+        scheme = self._run("model.layers.3.self_attn.kv_b_proj", True)
+        self.assertFalse(scheme.use_asm)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

There are two important improvements to make here:
1. Calling `.view(torch.uint8)` on `layer.weight.data` and `layer.weight_scale.data` can raise a `RuntimeError` if the tensors are not contiguous (e.g., due to slicing or sharding during tensor parallel loading). Calling `.contiguous()` first prevents this.
2. Recreating `layer.weight` and `layer.weight_scale` as plain `torch.nn.Parameter` objects discards their original custom parameter classes (`PackedvLLMParameter` and `GroupQuantScaleParameter`) and any associated custom attributes/metadata (such as `input_dim`, `output_dim`, `packed_dim`, etc.). This can break downstream components or tensor parallel communication that rely on these custom parameter types. Instead, update the parameter data in-place by assigning to `.data`.

```python
            weight = layer.weight.data.contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
            weight_scale = layer.weight_scale.data.contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
            weight = _asm_shuffle_weight(weight, layout=(16, 16))
            weight_scale = _asm_e8m0_shuffle(weight_scale)
            layer.weight.data = weight.contiguous()
            layer.weight_scale.data = weight_scale.contiguous()
```

If `self.use_asm` is `True` but `x` is a tuple (indicating a pre-quantized input), the code currently silently falls through to the Triton GEMM path. However, because the weights and scales have already been preshuffled for the ASM kernel during loading, running the Triton GEMM on these shuffled weights will produce completely incorrect results (silent correctness bug). We should explicitly assert or raise an error if `x` is a tuple when `self.use_asm` is enabled.

            out_features = layer.weight.shape[0]

                x = x.view(-1, x.shape[-1])

## Code Review

This pull request introduces an opt-in mechanism to route DeepSeek attention output projection (o_proj) layers through the aiter ASM a4w4 MXFP4 GEMM kernel on HIP devices when the SGLANG_DSR_OPROJ_MXFP4_ASM environment variable is enabled. The changes include weight preshuffling at load time, integration with the MLA forward path, and unit tests. The review feedback highlights critical improvements: ensuring weight and scale tensors are contiguous before viewing them, updating parameter data in-place to preserve custom parameter classes, asserting against unsupported pre-quantized tuple inputs in the ASM path to prevent silent correctness bugs, and using the idiomatic get_bool_env_var helper for environment variable parsing.
